critical_bugs: SyntaxError/Incomplete execution: The code is truncated mid-expression inside extract_session_features(), which will cause an immediate crash if executed.

Type mismatch risk: Timestamp arithmetic (observations[i]['timestamp_utc'] - observations[i-1]['timestamp_utc']) assumes numeric floats, but utc_now_iso() returns ISO strings. Mixing formats in sensor data pipelines will raise TypeError.

Arbitrary code execution via pickle.load(): Deserializing .pkl files without validation or allow-listing allows attackers to execute arbitrary Python code if a malicious file is placed in the persistent_knowledge directory.
warnings: Logic error in max_approach_speed_mps: Uses np.min() on approach speeds, which returns the most negative value (fastest retreat) instead of maximum approach speed.
Index desynchronization risk: Using 'continue' to skip high-speed glitches inside the observation loop may cause misalignment between position arrays and derived metrics if not carefully bounded.
Unsanitized root_path: os.path.join() does not validate or restrict root_path, potentially allowing path traversal if the parameter originates from external/untrusted sources.
recommendations: Replace pickle with JSON or msgpack for persistent storage to eliminate deserialization vulnerabilities. If pickle must be used, implement strict schema validation before load().
Standardize timestamp handling: Convert all timestamps to numeric Unix epoch floats at ingestion time before performing arithmetic operations.
Complete the truncated safety_events.append() block and add comprehensive unit tests for extract_session_features().
Fix approach speed calculation by using np.max(np.abs(approach_speeds)) or filtering positive values only.
Implement path canonicalization (os.path.realpath) and whitelist validation for root_path to prevent directory traversal.
